A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARLON and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations, 600-frame video comparisons, component ablations, inference-efficiency measurements, and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds resource measurements, training-data comparisons, and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: The latent VQ-VAE, autoregressive model, adaptive-normalization injection, training objective, and noise-resilient strategies remain unchanged. Describing three components instead of two and explaining overlapping generation more explicitly clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the training sources and VBench evaluation coverage. Table 5 varies amounts and combinations of existing OpenVid/Mixkit data, while 578-frame profiling remains long-video generation. Progressive prompts and reference-video conditioning in Figure 15 already appear in v1.

E2.justification: The ten short-video comparators, the FreeNoise/StreamingT2V/OpenSora long-video comparators, and the semantic-injection alternatives are retained. The added resource comparison uses OpenSora-V1.2, already compared for efficiency in v1; newly cited related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds resource profiling for 578-frame generation and a training-data comparison using 1M, 0.4M, and combined 0.7M configurations. These extend the experimental design without revising the retained VBench protocols, metrics, or principal training settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 substantially extend supplementary analysis with parameter, memory, and FLOP accounting and a training-data size/composition ablation. Figure 16 adds explicit failure cases involving makeup application and eating. The existing component ablations and denoising-step analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained uncertainty-sampling module is a training mechanism, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds resource results in Table 4, training-data results in Table 5, and failures in Figure 16. Newly reported imaging-quality scores include 59.15 for OpenVid-1M and 64.11 for 0.4M-only training; the combined-data row repeats Table 3. Retained benchmarks are mostly unchanged or rounded, although Show-1 Temporal Style changes from 25.28 to 25.2.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the autoregressive factorization, semantic injection, training loss, uncertainty sampling, and appendix diffusion preliminaries, are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and principal claims: combining AR and DiT models, noise-resilient conditioning, improved efficiency, outperforming OpenSora on eight of eleven metrics, and strong long-video generation.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 explicitly identifies backbone-dependent quality limits, impractical AR sequence lengths at 2K resolution, and failures in realistic hand movements. Appendices A.2–A.3 add interpretations of resource overhead and training-data quality/quantity. These materially expand the discussion of applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly documents component parameter counts, trainable versus frozen parameters, profiling with two 68-frame 512×512 clips on a 40GB A100, and the 17-frame overlap used to construct 578-frame videos. These are additional disclosures; the main implementation settings and project URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to StyleGAN-V, Phenaki, NUWA-XL, Yu et al. (2022), and Wang et al. (2023a). Section 3.2 expands positioning against sliding-window and diffusion-over-diffusion approaches, while retaining the existing research framing.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the introductory generation description, renames Section 2.2, presents long-video results before short-video results, and adds appendix subsections and acknowledgements. Most existing prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are revised, including a reorganized three-component framework diagram. Main comparisons and analysis displays are relocated; the short-video table gains rounded values, bold highlighting, and difference annotations. Tables 4–5 and failure-case Figure 16 are new, while earlier appendix examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The resource accounting in Table 4 makes the efficiency claim more assessable, while Table 5 and the explicit limitations and failures improve transparency. Clearer diagrams also help explain the unchanged method. These are useful supplementary gains, although the training-data comparison changes source/quality alongside size and therefore does not cleanly isolate their effects.
